headline: US stocks took a third straight gain on Meta's revenue beat and a near 8 percent jump in SpaceX, while Brent above 110 dollars, a 10 year Treasury yield near 5.15 percent and a December Fed increase close to fully priced left the Nifty lower for a second session with India VIX at a four month high.

summary.us: The S&P 500 rose 0.58 percent to 7,757.17 and the Nasdaq Composite 1.05 percent to 26,702.86 for a third straight advance, led by Nvidia up more than 2 percent and a near 8 percent jump in SpaceX after its first profit as a public company and Elon Musk's comment that a Tesla merger would be a good idea. After the close Meta reported revenue up 26 percent to 64.6 billion dollars and announced a 2-for-1 stock split, Tesla beat on adjusted earnings of 0.48 dollars but slipped on margin and AI spending questions, and the 10 year Treasury yield held near 5.11 to 5.15 percent with commentary putting December increase odds around 94 percent.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 fell 0.34 percent to 22,811.35 and the Bank Nifty 0.92 percent to 54,976.90 for a second straight decline as Brent above 110 dollars and continued foreign selling weighed, leaving the Nifty IT index up 2.52 percent as the only major gainer after Infosys and Wipro each added about 3 to 4 percent. ABB India and Siemens each dropped more than 5 percent in a capital goods selloff, Bajaj Finance fell 3.27 percent, State Bank of India slipped 1.1 percent after disclosing a suspected dark web leak of 3,897 customer records, the rupee traded near 94.71 a dollar, and the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO closed day one at about 3.2 times overall with institutions at 9.42 times and retail at 0.73 times.
summary.global: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 0.85 percent higher at 64,621.24 as AI names recovered from one month lows, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 0.90 percent to 23,651.87 and US listed China tech dropped sharply, with Alibaba down about 5 percent and Tencent's ADR off 4.1 percent on reports that ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have placed more than 35 billion dollars of Nvidia chip orders that may not all be filled. UK inflation came in hotter than expected at 3.5 percent in the year to September, the highest in a year, keeping the FTSE 100 close to flat, and Korea's Kospi was recovering after a 3.73 percent drop on October 20 that capped a slide of roughly 21 percent from its September high on doubts about AI capital spending.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to the cost of money rather than the promise of AI. Hot September CPI and PPI prints pushed fed funds futures toward pricing another quarter point increase by year end, and with the 10 year above 5 percent the market stopped asking whether AI compute is wanted and started asking who funds it: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit a record, the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell for eight straight sessions, and the Nasdaq shed 4.48 percent on the week while the Dow, carried by defensives, held a 0.67 percent gain. India went the other way, with the Nifty adding 3.44 percent as IT earnings landed well and the rupee rallied for six sessions on RBI intervention, even as October foreign outflows neared 50,000 crore rupees. Commodities split sharply, with WTI up 7.83 percent on a large US inventory draw and Strait of Hormuz risk while silver dropped 5.83 percent and gold was little changed, and crypto drifted lower on continued spot ETF outflows and close to a billion dollars of leveraged liquidations. Next week brings the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO, the largest in Indian history, alongside Tesla and Netflix earnings, Infosys on Friday and flash PMIs, all inside the Fed blackout that runs to the 28 October decision.

gspc.outlook_1y: Panmure Liberum set a year end 2027 target of 5,000 on October 5, 2026, arguing market resilience could unravel if bond yields and rates keep rising. Goldman Sachs raised its year end 2026 target to 8,000 from 7,600 in May 2026.
gspc.outlook_lt: Morgan Stanley's US equity strategist carried a mid 2027 target of 8,300 as of May 2026, based on expected 2027 earnings growth of 12 percent, and Wells Fargo Investment Institute's June 2026 table showed 8,600 to 8,800 for year end 2027. Analysts tracked by LSEG IBES expect index earnings growth to slow from 35 percent in 2026 to 15 percent in 2027, per an October 3, 2026 report.
